call_points.text: Meghalaya greenfield integrated plant is expected to be commissioned in the quarter ending 31 March 2028.
Blended cost of production rose to ₹4,636 per ton in Q2 against ₹4,329 in Q1.
Consolidated net cash at the group level stood at ₹8,168 crore as of Q2FY27.
FY27 cement volumes targeted at 40 million tonnes, including minor clinker sales.
FY27 capex guided at ₹1,500 crore, a slowdown from previous aggression.
Total cost increase of ₹150-200 per tonne expected in Q1FY27.
Meghalaya expansion involves 0.95 MT clinker and 0.99 MT cement capacity.
Premium products reached 22% of trade volume, up from 9% two years ago.
Demand saw a slight slowdown after April 15th following a steady start.
Net cash stands at ₹6,400 crore with gross debt of ₹1,500 crore.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Divisional Bench of the Hon'ble Rajasthan High Court vide Judgement dated 6th December, 2016 has allowed the appeal filed by Commercial Taxes Department/Finance Department of the Govt. of Rajasthan against earlier favorable order of single member bench of the Hon'ble Rajasthan High Court in the matter of incentives granted under Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme-2003 to the Company for capital investment made in cement plants in the State of Rajasthan. Vide the above Judgement of the Hon'ble High Court, the Company's entitlement towards Capital Subsidy for the entitled period stands revised from "up to 75% of Sales Tax / VAT" to "up to 50% of Sales Tax/ VAT". The Company has filed Special Leave Petition before the Hon'ble Supreme Court against the above judgment which is admitted for deciding on merits. The Commercial Taxes Department had issued notices seeking reply for recovering differential subsidy, the said notices have been challenged by the Company before Rajasthan High Court and High Court has stayed further proceedings by department against the Company. The Company has filed Special Leave Petition before the Hon'ble Supreme Court against the said judgment which is admitted for deciding on merits.

operating_notes.text: Total cement sale volume grew 11% YoY to 10.56 MT in Q4FY26.
Sales of premium products reached 22% of total trade volume in Q4FY26 compared to 16% in Q4FY25.
Installed cement capacity in India reached 69.3 MTPA following commissioning at Kodla, Karnataka.
Landed fuel cost per kcal was ₹1.60 in Q4FY26; guided to rise to ₹1.76-1.80 in Q1FY27.
Premium products share of trade volume reached 22% in Q4FY26.
Installed cement capacity in India reached 69.3 MTPA.
Fuel cost was ₹1.95/kcal in Q1FY27 vs contracted ₹1.82, with Pet Coke share at 9% and coal at 81%.
Trade sales mix fell to 62% from 71% and clinker conversion factor to 1.50 from 1.58 due to coal quality.
Net cash was ₹8,348 Cr in June 2026; RMC revenue ₹109 Cr with 26 operational plants.
Q2FY27 green electricity share stood at 65.2% of total consumption.
RMC network expanded to 35 plants (28 commercial) with Q2 revenue of ₹129 Cr.
Premium products contributed 28.7% of trade volumes in India operations in Q2FY27.
Green electricity accounted for 65.2% of total electricity consumption in Q2FY27 with 667 MW green generation capacity.
Landed fuel cost was ₹2.09/kCal in Q2FY27, up from ₹1.66 in Q2FY26 and ₹1.95 in Q1FY27.
Blended cost of production reached ₹4,636 per ton in Q2FY27 compared to ₹4,329 in Q1FY27.

timeline.summary: CRISIL reaffirmed the rating for Shree Cement's ₹1,000 crore commercial paper at A1+.
Shree Cement Limited’s Board, led by **S.S. Khandelwal**, recommended a final dividend of ₹70 per equity share (₹10 face value) for FY 2025-26, pending AGM approval on May 6, 2026.
Shree Cement commissioned 3.50 MTPA capacity in Karnataka and recommended a ₹70 final dividend for FY26.
Shyam Sundersigned by S.S. Khandelwal uploaded the earnings call recording for Q4FY26 on May 6, 2026, at shreecement.com.
Shree Cement guided for 40 MT volumes in FY27 and moderated its capex plan to ₹1,500 Cr.
Shree Cement received a ₹0.39 Cr GST demand order from the Assistant Commissioner, Pali, which it plans to appeal.
Shree Cement received a final income tax assessment order for FY2022-23 with a demand of ₹153.47 Cr, to be adjusted against pending refunds.
Shree Cement Limited’s Promoters/Promoter Group and persons acting in concert declared no encumbrance on their shares during FY2025-26 under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4).
On 14 October 2026, Shree Cement announced that its UAE subsidiary Shree Global FZE approved the incorporation of a step-down subsidiary in China named Shree International Trading (Shanghai) Limited.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹5,896.51 Cr (+23.8% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹261.82 Cr (-15.1% YoY).
Shree Cement reported Q2FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 24% YoY to ₹5,897 Cr
S.S. Khandelwal, Sunder Khandelwal uploaded earnings call recording for Q3FY27 on 23rd October 2026 via shreecement.com.
Shree Cement held its Q2FY27 earnings call, guiding for 40-41 MT FY27 volume and higher Q3 fuel costs of ₹2.15-2.20/kCal.
